content:
If you're not in a hurry to grab Apple's brand-new products on launch day and are willing to wait a bit, Apple's refurbished product store has always been a great option. Generally speaking, there's usually about a three-month wait between a product's release and when its refurbished version first appears on Apple's website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but it's worth noting that different platforms have varying quality standards and warranty terms……

Apple Certified Refurbished Products

Buying from the Apple Certified Refurbished store gets you roughly a 15% discount, and the products are essentially indistinguishable from brand-new units. Specifically, Apple promises all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing performed by Apple
  • Equipped with a brand-new outer shell, free of any scratches or wear
  • Equipped with a brand-new battery, offering the same battery life as a new device
  • All original accessories and cables included
  • Eligible for Apple's standard one-year warranty, with terms identical to brand-new products
  • Also eligible for purchasing AppleCare+

The only difference is that the product will come in a plain white cardboard box rather than the original retail packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed's pricing may be more competitive, but be aware that what you get won't come with the same guarantees in terms of condition:

  • Inspection and testing handled by the seller, not Apple
  • The outer shell is used and may have scratches or wear (see below for details)
  • The battery is used and only guaranteed to maintain at least 80% of its original capacity
  • Accessories may not be Apple original
  • Comes with a 90-day Amazon warranty rather than Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding scratches and wear, Amazon offers three tiers of quality classification:

  • Premium/Excellent: No visible cosmetic wear when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Light scratches, barely visible when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Acceptable: Scratches are clearly visible and can also be felt

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is far vaguer than Amazon about what your money actually gets you:

  • No commitments whatsoever regarding cosmetic condition, only claiming 'like-new performance and reliability'
  • Beyond the above statements, no specific information is provided about battery condition
  • No information is provided regarding accessories
  • Warranty is provided by the seller rather than Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while the Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only get 90 days. Their specific definitions for each tier are unclear.

9to5Mac Perspective

If you want a product that's indistinguishable from a brand-new unit in both condition and Apple warranty coverage, Apple's refurbished store is clearly the top choice.

However, Amazon Renewed's pricing can indeed be significantly cheaper, and if you're willing to accept the trade-offs listed above, you might find it to be a pretty good deal. Especially if you take our advice and go with the iPhone 17 Pro over this year's new model to save money (the only thing you'd be giving up is the cable), there are some quite attractive deals here:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (original price $1,499) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (original price $1,499) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (original price $1,499) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (original price $1,299) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (original price $1,299) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (original price $1,299) — just $1 short of hitting the all-time low price

As for Walmart Restored, I'd be concerned that their promises are just too vague, but the upside is that if you're not satisfied, you can opt for a return.
